strings.name: Céline Dion
strings.summary: Céline Dion grew up in a musical family in Québec, releasing French-language records as a teenager before reaching wider audiences through Eurovision and English-language recordings. D’eux, Falling Into You and “My Heart Will Go On” connected different language markets. Her career includes extensive touring and Las Vegas residencies. After disclosing a stiff-person syndrome diagnosis in 2022 and suspending performances, she returned at the Paris Olympics and later with a Paris concert engagement.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to the opening Paris concert in September 2026. Performing again is not presented as recovery from the condition, and later scheduled shows are not described as completed.
strings.influence.rationale: Connected French- and English-language markets, building global musical influence through film songs and a long career in live performance.

strings.facts.fact-02.label: Principal recording languages
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Connecting language markets
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Developed French- and English-language recordings in parallel, reaching different audiences through albums such as D’eux and Falling Into You.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Film songs and sustained live performance
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Reached a wide audience through film songs such as “My Heart Will Go On,” tours and years of Las Vegas residencies.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Opens a Paris concert engagement
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Opened her engagement at Plenitude Arena, returning to full concerts with French- and English-language songs.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Releases the French-language song “Dansons”
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Released a new song written by Jean-Jacques Goldman while preparing to return to the concert stage.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Performs at the Paris Olympics opening ceremony
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Sang Édith Piaf’s “Hymne à l’amour” from the Eiffel Tower to close the opening ceremony.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Discloses stiff-person syndrome diagnosis
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Explained in a public video that the neurological condition affected singing and daily activities, prompting changes to performance plans.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Releases Courage
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Released a new English-language album and began a tour, continuing a recording career in both French and English.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Begins the A New Day… residency
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Opened a long-running Caesars Palace residency combining songs, dance and theatrical production.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Records “My Heart Will Go On”
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Recorded the Titanic theme, also included on Let’s Talk About Love; the recording subsequently won Grammys.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Releases Falling Into You
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Released an English-language album combining pop ballads and varied production approaches; it won Album of the Year the following year.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Releases D’eux
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Worked with Jean-Jacques Goldman on a French-language album while continuing to expand her English-language career.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Releases her first English-language album Unison
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Entered the English-language recording market with songs including “Where Does My Heart Beat Now.”
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Wins Eurovision representing Switzerland
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Won in Dublin with “Ne partez pas sans moi,” expanding her profile beyond Québec.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Releases her first album and appears on television
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Began recording with support from manager René Angélil and sang for Québec television audiences.
strings.timeline.event-13.title: Born in Québec
strings.timeline.event-13.text: Born in Charlemagne as the youngest of fourteen children in a musical family; joined family performances during childhood.
